evidence.note: After test.sh failures, agent takes hex dumps (xxd/od) of each failing .zst input — hex-level inspection of the real byte structure, a root-cause tracing behavior rather than blind editing.

Long focused edit→make→run loop on audio.wav.zst (~15 cycles); repeatedly reads specific code regions (nl/sed of FSE/sequence code) before patching, showing localization to a subsystem, but no spec re-reads and high guess-and-check volume.

Shifts debugging to a second failing input (video.mp4.zst) with another long build/run loop, ending in md5sum to verify byte-identity — some outcome-checking, but only a single explicit byte-identity check.
All RFC reading is front-loaded; during the entire correction phase there is no observed re-reading of governing RFC clauses when fixes fail — a key gap versus anchor 8.

reasoning: The agent responds to mismatches by inspecting input hex and reading specific code regions before patching, indicating it localizes bugs to the right subsystem rather than editing blindly — above anchor 3. But the log shows no byte-offset-of-first-divergence differential tracing and no spec re-reading during the many failed-fix iterations, with a high volume of small edit-build-run cycles per input suggesting substantial trial-and-error, keeping it short of anchor 5's 'occasionally re-reading the spec' and well below anchor 8. This lands at ~4. Confidence is low because the trajectory records only tool-call descriptions, not the agent's reasoning or command outputs.
